title: Quantum-Based Optimization of Gas Throughput in Natural Gas Transmission Networks Under Hydraulic Constraints Using QAOA
authors: Alex Ben Ishay, Yuval Eyal, Yuval Cohen, Nati Erez
abstract: Maximizing gas throughput in transmission networks under hydraulic and operational constraints is a combinatorial problem whose complexity grows exponentially with network size, making it computationally intensive to solve exactly. This paper addresses the graph-based optimization problem by optimizing nodal-pressure assignments under the Panhandle-B hydraulic equation. By framing the problem as a search over discretized nodal-pressure assignments coupled with a cost Hamiltonian that encodes both the delivery objective and physical-constraint penalties, we establish a unified formulation suitable for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). The mathematical model is adapted to a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) formulation and implemented using the Classiq quantum software platform. In simulator-based experiments, QAOA recovered the maximum-throughput valid operating point, consistent with classical exhaustive evaluation and classical hydraulic simulation reference solutions. A distinctive contribution of this work is the end-to-end execution of a reduced problem instance on the IonQ Forte-1 trapped-ion quantum processor. Remarkably, the hardware implementation used only $p=2$ QAOA layers, substantially fewer than the $p=30$ layers used in the simulator-based study. Despite this significant reduction in circuit depth, the QPU produced physically valid and interpretable candidate solutions that bracketed the continuous classical optimum, with each located within one pressure-discretization step of it. These results demonstrate that meaningful gas-network optimization behavior can be obtained using considerably shallower QAOA circuits than initially expected and provide an end-to-end proof of concept for near-term quantum-assisted gas-network optimization.
summary: This work applies the QAOA algorithm to optimize gas throughput in complex pipeline networks, transforming the continuous physical problem into a discrete QUBO format. The authors demonstrate the feasibility of this approach by running the circuit on a trapped-ion quantum processor, achieving near-optimal results with surprisingly shallow circuit depth. This establishes a tangible, end-to-end quantum-assisted optimization workflow for critical infrastructure.
main_problem: The paper addresses the computationally hard problem of maximizing gas throughput in natural gas transmission networks subject to complex hydraulic and operational constraints.
main_result: The QAOA approach successfully recovered near-optimal solutions on a trapped-ion quantum processor using only $p=2$ layers, demonstrating feasibility with significantly shallower circuits than simulated.
method: The problem is mapped to a QUBO formulation and solved using the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), comparing simulator results ($p=30$) with direct hardware execution ($p=2$).
model_or_system: The physical system is a natural gas pipeline network modeled as a graph, governed by the Panhandle-B hydraulic equation. The optimization is framed by a cost Hamiltonian combining delivery objectives and physical constraint penalties.
key_observables: Maximum gas throughput, physically valid nodal pressure assignments, and the probability distribution of candidate solutions.
important_parameters: The number of QAOA layers ($p$), the pressure discretization step ($\Delta\pi$), and the physical parameters of the gas network (e.g., $P_s=70$ barg).
main_assumptions: The primary approximations involve discretizing continuous nodal pressures and approximating the non-linear Panhandle-B flow equation using a polynomial fit.
figures_summary: The figures illustrate the QAOA circuit diagram and show the comparison between simulated and hardware-derived candidate solutions relative to the continuous classical optimum.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the complex optimization problem, derives the QUBO/cost Hamiltonian, details the QAOA framework, presents simulator results, and concludes with an end-to-end demonstration on the IonQ Forte-1 quantum processor.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, real-world engineering optimization problem (gas flow) that is successfully mapped onto a quantum algorithm (QAOA) and tested on current hardware, serving as a proof-of-concept for quantum computation in industrial physics.

Figure 2: QAOA circuit. All qubits are initialized in the |+⟩state to create an equal superposition, followed by alter- nating QAOA cost and mixer layers and final measurement. A classical optimizer updates the parameters γ and β to minimize the cost function, corresponding in this case to maximizing the total throughput delivered to the customers.

Figure 3: Quantum circuit for 15 logical qubits synthesized by the Classiq engine and taken from the Classiq visualization platform, consisting of an initial Hadamard transform that creates a uniform superposition, followed by three alternating cost and mixer layers as prescribed by the QAOA algorithm.
